Thorn bushes on the side of the road hung over the top of an embankment, that crusted off into miniature avalanches sometimes. Below this on a crumbling road were two men and a woman walking downhill toward sparkling lights in the distance.

"Is that the next checkpoint?" Jonny asked.

"Uh-huh," said Kristen, bobbing her head.

The second man ahead of them did not say anything, Leonus, just as he had the previous couple years.

"You're always quieter around the guards, since we all met up after the asteroid fell," Jonny said, "what are you thinking about, Leo?"

"Nothing," said Leo.

Within a kilometer of the checkpoint gates, patrol guards in armored trucks pulled up in a circle round the group. A voice over the intercom system crackled, "What do'ya stragglers want at gate 578-E? Look at the cameras for identification, palms out."

Three camera-robots wheeled closer with zooming lens' adjusting.

Leo wore a brown tunic and hood over his head. Jonny called him an ancient Greek as their inside joke to each other. He removed the hood, there was a scar across his lips from a dog bite.

"You, Bryan, Leonus, your identification credentials in the network expired last month."

The patrol escorted them to a bunker under a hillside on the western side of the metal gate. The guards put them in separate isolation tanks, the size of individual coffins with injections every hour. Pulse charges attached to electronic skull caps monitored their brain waves while in the prison chambers.

"I want to go home," slurred Jonny from his coffin.

Leonus' isolation tank was pulled into a rectangular room, nurses placed him on a gurney strapped down with handcuffs, he squirmed. Robot metal arms shot drugs into his veins.

"I'll do anything, please," he cried out.

A deep voice on the intercom said: "Tell me your real name, the one you had before we failed to stop the asteroid that destroyed most of civilization."

"I don't know what you're talkin' about, they call me Leo, I was a Social Worker before the asteroid."

"No," said the voice in the empty room, Leo strapped to a gurney, "real name, and what you actually did as an occupation."

An electric saw turned on near his feet. At once he felt grinding metal pierce his skin, cutting off his toe.

"My name is Zoton, I wrote fiction before the accident."

The electric saw turned off.

"I think we can save your little toe, Zoton. I'm glad your memory returned," said the voice.

"Fuck off," Zoton said.

Two guards dragged Zoton out of the gurney, and pulled him into a holding room with a chair and table strapped to the ground. There were cameras to watch the prisoner from any possible angle.

"Zoton, are you awake?" a female voice said over the intercom.

He looked up after the guards walked away he was alone now. The drugs had knocked him out a few days. Blurry memories returned, the voice reminded him of someone familiar. An old friend.

"It's me, Kristen," said the voice from the intercom system. "You can trust me, Zoton, I know who you really are now. Walk out the door, you are free to leave anytime."

He looked up at the door, and then back at the table and chairs in the room. The table and chairs had disappeared replaced with darkness. He stood up, he examined what he thought was a room, stumbling in a damp room with a rocky floor.

This was not a room at all but a cave in the woods.

Zoton stepped out of the cave and saw city buildings nearby. The voices in his head were gone, the world had not ended from an astroid, as he thought someone told him.

He walked down to the city street, until he saw a few fellow bums in a circle, some old people he panhandled with with on Sprague Avenue last Summer, before the cops arrested them for public intoxication. One of them waved him over laughing as he chugged a bottle.

"Hey you guys, it's Zoton, know where I can get a drink around here?"

"Boy, take a sip from this, some real fire, tell ya what now," said old man Higgins, handing him a half-empty whiskey bottle.

Zoton walked the neon drenched streets that night, looking one by one into a small mom and pop shop window, a Salvation Army, financial buildings, a bank that burned down. He covered up with a hoodie jacket donated from a Church last month in a garage sale, tattered socks without shoes.

A police siren behind the man echoed, lights swinging different shades of red and blue across a lawn.

"You, yeah you, put your hands up and get on the ground. Stop, I said!"

The cop raised his gun and fired a shot in his direction, cutting through the man's lungs. A small spot of crimson red formed a circle on his back as he fell to the ground.

It was July 16th 2031. We had detected an asteroid with the size of ~150 kilometers from the Kuiper Belt. It's amazing how no one had noticed before.

After careful work by all governments in Earth, and the small settlement on Mars consisting of ~1000 scientists and astronauts, they have reached a consensus that the asteroid will impact Earth within about five years. Mass hysteria happened. People preached about God in the streets, people fight for food, people fight for basic needs. Nothing matters anymore. Money is worthless.

In about four years, the governments have made multiple large rockets carrying multiple artificial habitats. They had about ~450 rockets. Anything they can carry, such as technology and foods were brought in. On March 26th 2035, they launched all rockets at once. These 450 rockets were key to human survival. Most of the poor humans were unable to go as the seats on the rockets weren't that much and it was expensive. Out of 12 billion that lived on Earth, only 2.5 billion made it out.

On September 2035, the asteroid impacted Earth. The asteroid was faster than anticipated. 9.5 billion souls died in a blink of the eye. It was one of the largest explosions in living memory.

And that takes us to now, Sol 24th in the month of August. The human race have populated the entirety of Mars with the population of five billion souls.

IAMA Recovery Agent (in-house collections) for one of Canada's "Big Five" banks AMAA

• How far are you legally able to go to, you know, "encourage" repayment of debt?

  • Are there any other, shall we say, not necessarily illegal, but "dirty" tactics you can use to get back debts?

Disclaimer* The laws and policies in Canada regarding debt collection will be quite different from other countries.

  • Legally, and by bank policy, I have the authority to assign accounts to third party collection agencies, recommend the outsource Mortgages for Power of Sale or Foreclosure with one of our legal partners, recommend the repossession of, or release of a lien on a vehicle or other chattel, negotiate and authorize lump sum settlements on unsecured debts, and place calls to the debtors residence in order to initiate contact, and demand repayment in part or in full of their credit facilitates. I can close credit cards, reduce overdraft limits, place holds on your bank account, offset (take) money from an account in order to offset debts, and much more.

I am obligated by the Privacy Act of Canada to only discuss banking matter directly with the debtor, or legally appointed Power of Attorney, and so I cannot call their spouses, friends, family members etc. except to leave a message for the debtor. Aside from that, I can "legally" collect pretty much however I want, but I am heavily constrained by the bank itself who understandably wants to keep its clients and limit PR concerns. Most often, I'm calling a debtor, advising them of their delinquency, and trying to arrange repayment in order to avoid all of the above outcomes.

 

  • No illegal/dirty tactics, that's the third party collection agency's job

Do you enjoy your job? Do you do well for yourself?

Thanks for the AMA :)

It's a job. I'm thankful I'm not in the same situation as some of our clients. I do well for myself. Salaried position with some clout in a large organization with lots of room for movement. Medical benefits, pension plan, and employee shared ownership program. Basic bank employee deal, but several rungs higher up from your average teller.
